dialogue.origin: 今日は。本日は、宜しくお願い致します。
dialogue.content: Hello. Thank you for coming in today. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.origin: よろしくお願いします
dialogue.content: Thank you. Likewise.

dialogue.origin: 時間になりましたら始めさせていただきます。
dialogue.content: We will begin once it's time.

dialogue.origin: 今日は。相談員です。本日は相談にお越しいただきありがとうございます。最初に年齢と性別を教えて頂けますでしょうか。
dialogue.content: Hello. I'm your counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. To begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.origin: 40代、男性。大学生の長男について、だらしがないので、イライラしてます
dialogue.content: I'm a man in my 40s. I'm frustrated with my eldest son, who is in college, because he's so sloppy.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか。親からしてみるとだらしなく見えることが多くありますね。
dialogue.content: I see. From a parent's perspective, many things can come across as sloppy.

dialogue.origin: どのような、ところがイライラするのか差し支えなければお話して頂けますか。
dialogue.content: If you don't mind, could you tell me what specific things you find frustrating?

dialogue.origin: まず、部屋がゴミ箱状態。何度言っても掃除しない。してもすぐゴミ箱に戻る。挨拶できない。コミュニケーション上もかなり課題あり。
dialogue.content: First of all, his room is like a garbage dump. No matter how many times I tell him, he won't clean it. Even if he does, it goes right back to being a mess. He can't greet people properly, and he has significant communication issues.

dialogue.origin: それは、親としても困った問題ですね。
dialogue.content: I can see how that would be a troubling problem for you as a parent.

dialogue.origin: 本人は、どう思っているか、お話はされていますか。
dialogue.content: Have you talked with him about how he sees it?

dialogue.origin: 厳しく注意しても、嫌々な感じで仕方なくその場を乗り切る感じで変えていこうという気がありません
dialogue.content: Even when I scold him harshly, he just acts reluctant and does the bare minimum to get through the moment. He has no intention of changing.

dialogue.origin: 親として厳しく言わなければならない場面がありますよね。どこの家の子もお父さんに叱られるのを恐れますしね。
dialogue.content: As a parent, there are times when you have to be strict, aren't there? Children in any household tend to be afraid of being scolded by their father.

dialogue.origin: 失礼ですがお子様は、何人兄弟ですか。
dialogue.content: Forgive me for asking, but how many children do you have?

dialogue.origin: 2人兄妹で。下に妹がいます。
dialogue.content: I have two children. He has a younger sister.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか。ご長男の振る舞いに対して奥様も注意なさったりされていますか。
dialogue.content: I see. Does your wife also say anything to him about his behavior?

dialogue.origin: しますが、妻の言うことはあまり真剣に聞こうとしませんね。妻も昔から長男には口うるさく言うので、本人にとっては「あーまたなんか言ってるわ、、」程度にしか捉えていません
dialogue.content: She does, but he doesn't really listen seriously to what she says. My wife has always nagged him, so to him, it's just, "Oh, she's at it again..." and he tunes it out.

dialogue.origin: そうですね。私の家も同じでしたね。母親の言うことを聞かずにいたので、「お父さんから何か言ってよ！」でしたね。
dialogue.content: I understand. It was the same in my house. My children wouldn't listen to their mother, so it was always, "You have to say something to them!"

dialogue.origin: 我が家の長男も部屋を汚し放題にしていた時がありましたね。次男もですが。
dialogue.content: There was a time when my eldest son's room was an absolute mess, too. My second son as well.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですよ。私が厳しく言うと一瞬締まりますが、とにかく甘やかし過ぎたのかもしれません。
dialogue.content: Exactly. When I'm strict with him, he shapes up for a moment, but perhaps we've spoiled him too much.

dialogue.origin: 妹の長女は、しっかりしてて明るく性格も良いので、、真逆です
dialogue.content: My younger daughter is responsible, cheerful, and has a good personality... she's the complete opposite.

dialogue.origin: そんな時は、私も育て方を間違えたかな？と思ったりしました。
dialogue.content: At times like that, I also wondered if I had raised them the wrong way.

dialogue.origin: 我が家の娘もそうでした。お兄ちゃん二人をぎゃふんと言わせるのがうまかったです。
dialogue.content: My daughter was the same. She was good at putting her two older brothers in their place.

dialogue.origin: やっぱり女の子の方が奇麗好きなのでしょうね。
dialogue.content: I suppose girls tend to be neater.

dialogue.origin: 普通に、会話が出来るので、安心感あります。もちろん、まだまだ未熟なところも多いですが。長男は暗すぎるので、、それもイライラするんです
dialogue.content: I can have a normal conversation with her, which is reassuring. Of course, she's still immature in many ways. But my son is just too gloomy... and that frustrates me too.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか。お父さんがイライラするのは、疲れますよね。仕事もありますし。
dialogue.content: I see. It must be exhausting for you as a father to be so frustrated, especially with work to deal with as well.

dialogue.origin: 一度、そのイライラを封印してご長男と向き合ってみてはいかがでしょうか。
dialogue.content: Perhaps you could try setting that frustration aside for a moment and connecting with your son.

dialogue.origin: どんな感じに向き合えば良いですか
dialogue.content: How should I approach him?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。まず、ご自分の青春時代はどうだったかを思い出してみてはいかがでしょうか？『男とは』こうなんだ、なんて思いこんだことはございませんでしたか。
dialogue.content: Well, how about you start by remembering what you were like in your youth? Were there ever times you had your own fixed ideas about 'what it means to be a man'?

dialogue.origin: ご自身の青春時代とご長男を比べながら、感情は抜きで話をしてみると本音が聞けるかもしれません。
dialogue.content: If you talk to him while comparing your own youth with his, but setting emotions aside, you may be able to hear his true feelings.

dialogue.origin: 今の時代の子なので、、男とは、というのも微妙ですね。でも、ご提案はありがとうございます
dialogue.content: He's a kid of this generation, so the whole 'what it means to be a man' thing is a bit tricky. But thank you for the suggestion.

dialogue.origin: 実はいま考えてるのは、ひとり暮らしさせたいと思ってて、要は早く自立して、苦労を経験させたいなと。本人にとっても良い選択かと。
dialogue.content: Actually, what I'm thinking now is that I want him to live on his own. Basically, I want him to become independent quickly and experience some hardship. I think it would be a good choice for him, too.

dialogue.origin: すみません。出しゃばりすぎですね。方法は色々あると思いますが、私は、とにもかくにも感情抜きで話をすることを心がけました。
dialogue.content: I'm sorry, I may have overstepped. I'm sure there are many ways to approach this, but for me, I made a point to speak without letting my emotions get in the way, no matter what.

dialogue.origin: 我が家の子どもは、男の部屋は汚くて当たり前、なんてドラマなどをみて勝手に想像していたようです。
dialogue.content: My kids seemed to have gotten the idea from TV shows and the like that it's normal for a boy's room to be messy.

dialogue.origin: 一人暮らしの選択もありですね。
dialogue.content: Having him live on his own is certainly an option.

dialogue.origin: 我が家の子どもたちの意識が変わったのは、友人が訪ねてくるようになってからですね。
dialogue.content: My children's mindset changed once friends started visiting.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。うちの息子は友達少なくそういうのないんですよ
dialogue.content: I see. My son doesn't have many friends, so that sort of thing doesn't happen.

dialogue.origin: 遊び呆けて、家に帰ってこないくらいやんちゃなくらいが　ほんとはいいんですが。贅沢な悩みですかね
dialogue.content: To be honest, I'd rather he be a little wild, fooling around and not coming home. Is that too much to ask for?

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか。娘の友人が遊びに来ることが多くなって、妹からお兄ちゃんたちの部屋が汚くて皆に笑われた。と言われたあたりにきちんと片付けるようになってきたと思います。汗臭いとも言われてました。
dialogue.content: I see. When my daughter's friends started coming over more often, she told her brothers that their rooms were messy and everyone laughed at them. I think that's when they started to clean up properly. She also told them they smelled sweaty.

dialogue.origin: 子どもは、子どもなりに考えていますよ。親子の会話が成り立っていれば心配はないと思います。遅い反抗期と思ってもいいのではないでしょうか。
dialogue.content: Children think in their own way. As long as you can have a conversation as parent and child, I don't think you need to worry. Perhaps you could see it as a late rebellious phase.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。ご経験の中でのお話は参考になります。
dialogue.content: I see. Hearing about your personal experiences is very helpful.

dialogue.origin: 相談員さん、すみませんが急用が入ったため、これにて終了とさせていただけますか。少し時間早いですが。
dialogue.content: Counselor, I'm sorry, but something urgent has come up. Could we end the session here? I know it's a little early.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます。出しゃばりすぎて申し訳ありません。子を思うのは親として当然ですし、ひょっとすると親がイライラするのをみて楽しんでいるのかもしれません。自分のほうが大人だと言わんばかりに。
dialogue.content: Thank you. I apologize if I was too forward. It's only natural for a parent to worry about their child, and it's possible he might be enjoying seeing you frustrated, as if to say he's the more mature one.

dialogue.origin: こちらこそありがとうございました。今日はこちらで失礼します。勉強になりました。
dialogue.content: No, thank you very much. I'll be leaving now. This has been very enlightening.

dialogue.origin: 承知しました。もし、何か不安なことがございましたら、また相談にお越しください。別のスタッフが対応いたしますが本日の内容は、引き継がせていただきます。本日は、お忙しい中、相談にお越しいただきありがとうございました。終了させていただきます。
dialogue.content: Understood. If you have any other concerns, please feel free to come back for another session. A different staff member will assist you, but I will make sure today's discussion is passed on. Thank you for coming in today despite your busy schedule. We will now conclude the session.

dialogue.origin: ロールプレイを終了させていただきます。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: This concludes the role-play. Thank you very much.

topic.sub: 長男とのコミュニケーション問題
